reading.body:
Data Felix DF01 in Caserta, Italy, is tagged as a data center in OpenStreetMap but cannot be independently verified as operational or its capacity determined from public sources.

The facility's naming convention, which includes an explicit alphanumeric code (DF01) matching a pattern used by genuine data-center operators to identify individual buildings within portfolios, suggests it may be a real small facility. Southern Italy hosts regional and municipal hosting providers despite being a less developed data-center market than the north. However, no operator website, business registration, or press coverage could be confirmed during this research session, leaving operator identity, power capacity, and service offering unknown.

This entry demonstrates a gap common in smaller data-center markets: plausible facilities identified through infrastructure tagging but lacking the public documentation trail of larger operations. Without confirmed megawatt capacity or operator details, this location cannot yet be weighted in assessments of regional compute availability or power demand.
